plan.contextChunk: This figure is an annotated graph of one full cycle of a transformed sine wave, marked up to expose its midline, amplitude, and period. The vertical y-axis carries ticks from -2 up to 4, the horizontal x-axis is labeled at pi/2 and at pi, and both axes end in arrowheads. The solid dark blue curve leaves the y-axis at height 1, rises to a maximum of 4 a quarter of the way along, falls back through that starting height, bottoms out at -2 near three-quarters of the way, and returns to height 1 at pi. A horizontal orange arrow at the level y = 1 extends rightward from the vertical axis, labeled Midline: y = 1. A vertical teal arrow runs up the curve's peak from that orange level to the maximum, tagged by a leader with Amplitude: |A| = 3. Below the plot, a red double-headed arrow spans the width of the drawn cycle beneath the label Period = pi. The three annotations measure independent things: the vertical center of the oscillation, the stretch away from that center, and the horizontal distance before the shape repeats. Taken together they are the quantities needed to reconstruct the equation of a sinusoid from its picture alone.

interactionPlan.concept: A sinusoid is fully determined by three independent measurements read off its graph: the midline (vertical center), the amplitude (vertical distance from midline to peak), and the period (horizontal length of one repeat).
elements: vertical y-axis with arrowhead and integer tick labels from -2 to 4
horizontal x-axis with arrowhead and tick labels at pi/2 and pi
dark blue sinusoid curve y = 1 + 3*sin(2x) drawn over one full cycle from x=0 to x=pi (starts at y=1, peaks at 4, troughs at -2, returns to 1)
orange horizontal arrow at y = 1 extending rightward from the y-axis, labeled 'Midline: y = 1'
teal vertical double-headed arrow from the midline (y=1) up to the curve's peak (y=4), with a leader line to the label 'Amplitude: |A| = 3'
red horizontal double-headed arrow below the x-axis spanning x=0 to x=pi, labeled 'Period = pi'

interactions.label: Amplitude |A|
interactions.teaches: Amplitude is the vertical distance from the midline to the peak (and to the trough); dragging it moves the peak and trough symmetrically away from or toward the midline while the midline itself stays put.

interactions.label: Midline y = D
interactions.teaches: The midline is the vertical center of the oscillation; shifting it translates the entire wave up or down without changing how far the peaks reach from that center, separating vertical shift from amplitude.

interactions.label: Period P
interactions.teaches: The period is the horizontal distance over which the wave completes one full cycle and begins to repeat; stretching or compressing it changes the wave's horizontal spacing, not its height.

demo_steps.title: Read the three quantities
demo_steps.narration: The annotated curve shows midline y = 1 (orange), amplitude 3 (teal, midline-to-peak), and period pi (red, one full cycle). Together these three numbers reconstruct the equation y = 1 + 3*sin(2x).

demo_steps.title: Change the amplitude
demo_steps.narration: Drag the amplitude slider: the peak and trough move symmetrically away from or toward the orange midline, which does not move. Amplitude is purely a vertical stretch about the midline.

demo_steps.title: Shift the midline
demo_steps.narration: Now drag the midline slider: the whole wave rides up or down with the orange line while the teal peak-to-midline distance stays fixed, showing vertical shift is independent of amplitude.

demo_steps.title: Stretch the period
demo_steps.narration: Finally drag the period slider: the red span widens or narrows and the wave completes one cycle over the new horizontal distance, leaving its height untouched. Period controls horizontal repeat, not vertical size.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Midline, amplitude, and period measure three orthogonal things — vertical center, vertical stretch, and horizontal repeat — and each can be changed without affecting the others, which is exactly why three numbers suffice to write the sinusoid's equation.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Plot one cycle of y = D + A*sin((2*pi/P)*x) over x in [0, P]. Default D=1, A=3, P=pi gives the textbook curve (start y=1, peak 4 at x=pi/4, trough -2 at 3*pi/4, back to 1 at pi). Dark blue thick curve; orange horizontal arrow at y=D labeled 'Midline: y = D'; teal vertical double-headed arrow from y=D to the peak labeled 'Amplitude: |A| = A'; red horizontal double-headed arrow beneath the axis spanning [0,P] labeled 'Period = P'. Keep each annotation's color matched to its slider so the link is obvious. Auto-scale the y-axis as D and A change so the curve and arrows stay in view; keep x-axis tick labels updating to P/2 and P. Arrowheads on both axes as in the source.

Inspecting the graph, we can determine that the period is π, the midline is y=1, and the amplitude is 3. See the figure.

A graph of y=3sin(2x)+1. The graph has an amplitude of 3. There is a midline at y=1. There is a period of pi. Local maximum at (pi/4, 4) and local minimum at (3pi/4, -2).
